analysis:
The only change is a documentation-only addition to docs/reference/configuration.md (head line 414): a table row for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED. It describes a Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel selector for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35 models, read once per process and forwarded to the LaunchAgent. No executable code, auth, attestation, encryption, billing or wire-protocol behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

Threat-model relevance: the row touches the inference engine boundary (TB-007). The doc says the default probe keeps the four-row kernel only where it bit-matches gated_delta_step, and that forced kernels (`packed`/`rows`) skip that check and are for A/B measurement only. That is a correctness/integrity knob, not a confidentiality control. Decode, MTP verification and masked updates always use the stock kernel. It is relevant to T-007 (output manipulation) and T-056 (not a claim of correct computation) only in that a provider operator could force an unchecked kernel. That is already within the accepted malicious-provider model, and the env var is operator-local.

The claimed LaunchAgent forwarding is a statement about the underlying source change, which was not supplied: LaunchAgent.swift passthrough lists and GatedDelta.swift are not in this batch. So I cannot verify the forwarding claim, the parsing semantics, or the bit-exact probe. The forwarding claim also means forced-kernel settings persist into installed daemons, which the next pass should compare against the allowlist code if that source change is part of the PR. The doc text itself introduces no new attack surface. The doc also does not interact with the prefix-cache threat T-041, and no cache keys, salts or at-rest formats are mentioned.

Base_text units 2 and 3 are the unchanged surrounding doc; I checked them for contradictions with the new row and found none.
